findings.title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider.order() is added to the interface without a default implementation. Any third-party or downstream implementation of CryptoProvider (this is a public SPI, e.g. custom FIPS/non-FIPS providers) will fail to compile/run against this version with 'does not override order()'. Since ServiceLoader instantiation fails with ServiceConfigurationError, previously-working deployments will break at runtime. A default value (e.g. default int order() { return 0; }) should preserve compatibility.

findings.title: Providers with equal order() have nondeterministic selection; multi-provider error removed
findings.body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order() == 200. The previous code threw an IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was found, forcing operators to fix the classpath; now detectProvider silently picks one. When two providers with the same order are present (e.g. default and elytron, or default and fips1402), ServiceLoader ordering is classpath-dependent and effectively arbitrary, so a deployment can silently get the wrong crypto provider (e.g. non-FIPS provider in a FIPS environment) with no error or warning beyond a debug log. Either the orders should differ per provider, or ties should be rejected/logged at warn level.

findings.title: Most CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking signed-JWT client credentials in authz-client
findings.body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider is installed as the only CryptoProvider on a plain authz-client classpath (via the new META-INF/services file), but getSignature, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, getAesCbcCipher/GcmCipher, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory etc. all throw UnsupportedOperationException. The authz-client JWT client-credentials flow (Http/TokenCallable using JWTClientCredentialsProvider in keycloak-core) signs the client assertion via CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(...) and related calls, and token verification/PemUtils paths call getPemUtils(). A user who adds only keycloak-authz-client and configures 'signed_jwt' credentials (or any feature touching the unsupported methods) will now get UnsupportedOperationException instead of the previously-working default JCA behavior. These methods should return JCA defaults (Signature.getInstance(...), KeyFactory.getInstance(...), etc.) rather than throwing.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider, not a BC provider
findings.body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which on a stock JVM is the SUN provider (or whatever is configured). Callers of this method (e.g. code that derives algorithm names or provider behavior from 'the BouncyCastle provider') will silently operate on an unrelated provider; returning null would be more honest than masquerading the SUN provider as BouncyCastle.

findings.title: Indefinite-length BER sequences silently decode as an empty element list
findings.body: readLength() returns -1 for the indefinite-length encoding (0x80), and readSequence()'s 'while (length > 0)' loop then exits immediately, returning an empty list with no error. asn1derToConcatenatedRS will report the misleading 'Invalid sequence with size different to 2' instead of a proper parse error. Indefinite-length input should be rejected explicitly (or handled), since this decoder otherwise claims DER support.

findings.title: ECDSA test does not verify the DER output against the original signature
findings.body: The test converts DER->concat->DER->concat and asserts the two concatenated forms match, but never asserts that the round-tripped DER equals the original 'sign' bytes, nor that the recovered r/s values actually verify against the public key. A bug that corrupts both conversions symmetrically (e.g. wrong offset handling for a fixed input) would still pass. Adding Assert.assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des) or a Signature.initVerify check would strengthen it.

findings.title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances and write r/s into them, then discard the results; only the encoders used in writeDerSeq at lines 117-121 matter. The dead statements are confusing and should be removed.
